subject: Unplanned runtime patch — brief maintenance window and customer coordination
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 02:15:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Unplanned runtime patch (short window)

Team —

SRE caught a memory fragmentation pattern this morning that can cascade into elevated tail latency and occasional OOMs for long-sequence customers using KV-cache. We have a low-risk, out-of-band patch (runtime patch v1.2.3) that mitigates the allocator path.

Planned action: apply patch to a small subset of hosts now (rolling, <30min impact window). We anticipate brief 503s for inflight batching slots and a small chance of client-visible latency blips during key eviction.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: please prepare a customer-facing note and send to active customers that might be impacted (I will draft).
- Lauren: coordinate with Legal/Procurement if we need any immediate contract notices for customers on strict SLA clauses.
- SRE: I will lead the rollout and post-rollout verification. Patch attached for reference (text diff).

Attachments: runtime_patch_v1.2.3.patch.txt

I will follow with the external notice in ~10 minutes.

Ben
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Akira Sato <akira@vertex-analytics.com>, procurement@vertex-analytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 02:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Unplanned runtime patch — brief maintenance window and customer coordination

Akira / Vertex team —

I wanted to let you know about an unscheduled, short-notice maintenance action we are performing for a small slice of runtime hosts to mitigate an emergent memory fragmentation issue that can surface for long-context workloads. We are rolling a targeted hotpatch across affected kernels now.

Impact summary:
- Window: immediate; expected completion within 20–30 minutes of this email.
- Customer impact: transient 503s for in-flight batched requests in rare cases; briefly elevated latency for a small fraction of tokens during eviction. No loss of persisted user data is expected.
- Action required from you: for the next 30 minutes, please avoid submitting large synchronous batch inference jobs if possible. If you cannot pause, let us know and we will prioritize your tenant for a safe-roll schedule.

We will:
- Monitor your tenant endpoints closely and revert/rollback if we observe significant customer impact.
- Share a concise postmortem and the rollback steps within 24 hours.

Attachments: rollback_steps.md (high-level rollback and verification checklist)
Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721 (incident ticket)

If you have immediate questions or need a voice call, reply all and we will hop on a bridge.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0112

Thanks for the heads up, Ben. We can pause scheduled batch runs, but we have some long-running feature extraction jobs that are difficult to stop mid-flight. A couple of questions:

1) If we see elevated error rates during the window, will that count against the monthly SLA?
2) Do you provide access to the relevant request logs / span traces for our engineers to correlate during the window?

If you prefer, we can escalate to an immediate call; otherwise we’ll pause non-essential batches and monitor.

—
Akira Sato
Platform Engineering Manager
Vertex Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Akira Sato <akira@vertex-analytics.com>, procurement@vertex-analytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 04:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unplanned runtime patch — brief maintenance window and customer coordination

Akira —

Appreciate the quick reply. Answers inline: 

1) SLA treatment: outages or degraded performance caused by this emergent mitigation will not count against monthly SLA for tenants where we performed the targeted patch; we will pro-rate credits where appropriate. Lauren — please follow up with Procurement and record the exception.

2) Logs & traces: yes — we will grant Vertex temporary read-only access to the tenant traces for the 2-hour window surrounding the patch. Marissa, can you share the (short-lived) trace access link and the span ids we are monitoring?

Postmortem & next steps:
- We will produce a short postmortem within 24 hours describing root cause, fixed paths, and longer-term mitigation. Ticket: INF-4721.
- Internal owners: SRE (Vivek Kulkarni) will own rollout verification; Reliability lead (Ben Carter) owns customer communications; Customer Success (Marissa Cole) will run the postmortem sync.
- Offer: if there is measurable SLA impact, we will issue a usage credit and a one-time operational consultation to help Vertex tune their batching profile.

Proposed follow-up call: Today 09:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.

Ben
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
